text:
maya: quick scan of quark14b bring-up (summary): int8 perf reduces per-token cost ~38-45% vs fp16 on our 8k-chat slices, avg latency +8ms, but we see a 5-7% drop in multi-turn recall on GTN prompt set. full numbers below.

sam: can you paste the slice breakdown? curious which prompts regress most.

maya: sure — topline by slice (3-turn convs):
- short Q/A: cost -42%, recall +/-0%
- multi-step reasoning: cost -45%, recall -7%
- instruction-following (long): cost -38%, recall -5%

lorenzo: interesting. does the regression correlate with KV cache hit pattern? maybe int8 KVC has more noise.

audrey: did we run hybrid soft-fallback (int8->fp16 on low-confidence spans)? any quality recovery?

maya: yes, ran a small routing pilot: fallback on predicted low-confidence tokens (model score threshold 0.18) — recovered ~60% of the recall loss but increased cost back ~12% (net cost saving still ~25%). patch config below:

```json
{"routing":{"policy":"confidence-fallback","threshold":0.18,"fallback_model":"quark14b-fp16"}}
```

sam: that seems promising. How about latency tail with fallback? tail p95/p99 numbers?

maya: p95 +20ms with fallback, p99 +45ms. baseline fp16 p99 was 280ms; int8 w/o fallback p99 ~265ms; int8 w/ fallback p99 ~325ms (spikes on routed requests).

lorenzo: do we have unit-econ calc for expected traffic mix? product cares about $/1000 messages for the chat feature.

maya: rough calc (per 1k requests, mixed slices from GTN sample):
- fp16 baseline: $4.20 per 1k
- int8 straight: $2.45 per 1k
- int8 + fallback: $3.05 per 1k

numbers assume current infra pricing and observed token distributions.

audrey: product question: is the residual recall drop in int8 acceptable for GTN power users? we should surface metric to PMs: recall delta by persona.

sam: agree. also need to run targeted prompt priming tests — many regressions look priming-sensitive. maybe small prompt-rewrite recovers quality on cost-friendly variant.

maya: did a 150-sample priming probe: templated system prompt tweak recovered ~40% of the recall loss in multi-step slice without fallback. low-cost hack.

lorenzo: nice. can you add that to the playbook? two levers: routing fallback (ops) and prompt priming (product/prompt engineering).

eval-bot: quick note: CI evals updated -> added quark14b-int8 checkpoints + fallback scenarios to the nightly regression suite.

audrey: next steps from product-side: run a  week-long canary at 10% traffic with int8+priming, monitor recall delta by user-cohort, and cost savings. escalate to dedicated reserved if stable.

maya: action items: 1) maya -> push priming recipes + examples to repo (PR) 2) sam -> plan 10% canary and tracking dashboard 3) lorenzo -> verify KVC behavior on longer contexts 4) audrey -> sync with PMs and create cohort gating. I'll drop the short scorecard in the doc channel after PR.

sam: lgtm. small note: include runbook for rollback (we already have model-pin route + immediate fp16 fallback flag). :thumbsup:

lorenzo: adding: watch for latency p99 spikes during peak; ops may need extra headroom for fallback bursts.

maya: thanks all. posting brief scorecard next: includes slice-level delta, econ table, and recommended default (int8+priming, canary, fallback enabled).
